reason: V77 is the most useful fresh comparison because it keeps strong broad separated plates and a good Stegosaurus body, but its tail still overcounts the thagomizer. V75 and V76 have similarly strong plate mass but clearly show too many tail spikes, and V76 also risks leaf-vein plate surfaces. Keep v6 first until broad separated plates and exactly four thagomizer spikes pass in the same image.
rejectIfPromoting: tail tip shows fewer or more than exactly four large spikes
plates read as leaves, leaf veins, fins, or a connected sail
plate row becomes a single wall without visible gaps
legs or feet are hidden enough to block quadruped count
body drifts toward ankylosaur, turtle, sauropod, or theropod anatomy
